faq.question: How much does an AI browser agent cost per task?
faq.answer: A typical managed browser-agent task with 6–12 steps costs $0.05–$0.40 in LLM + browser compute, depending on model choice, screenshot resolution, and retries. Self-hosted stacks can cut compute cost but add infrastructure labor.

faq.question: Which is the cheapest browser infrastructure provider?
faq.answer: Browser Use Cloud advertises browsers from $0.02/hr, the cheapest metered option. Skyvern bundles AI + browser at $0.05 per step. TinyFish starts at $0.015 per step or ~$0.00375 per minute. Self-hosted is variable but can be cheapest at scale if you already run the servers.

faq.question: How much does Computer Use cost with Claude vs Gemini?
faq.answer: Computer use is billed by LLM tokens, and each screenshot adds 1,000–2,000 image tokens. A 10-step task with 720p screenshots usually costs $0.05–$0.15 with Claude Sonnet and $0.02–$0.08 with Gemini Flash. OpenAI Operator is a flat $200/month subscription.

faq.question: How do retries affect cost?
faq.answer: Retries multiply cost. If your success rate is 85%, roughly 15% of tasks fail and need a retry, raising effective cost by 15% or more. Use shorter tasks, lower screenshot resolution, and simpler UIs to reduce failure-driven retries.

faq.question: What resolution should I use for screenshots?
faq.answer: 1280×720 is a good default: detailed enough for most UI elements but cheaper than 1920×1080. Lower resolutions reduce image tokens but can miss small buttons or dense dashboards.
